summary: Tested CareFlow booking APIs and mobile UI. Health and doctors endpoints passed; authenticated mobile booking, 14-date calendar, live slots, confirmation, close dialog, and overflow checks passed. One real mobile navigation usability issue was observed when the sidebar link is interacted with while hidden. Existing regression booking tests returned 409 because their fixed slots were already occupied.

minor.issue: Two existing regression tests expected a fresh fixed slot but received the intended 409 conflict because the slot was already booked by persisted test/demo data.

ui_bugs.issue: Find a doctor link is outside the viewport while the sidebar is closed; direct click cannot work until the menu is opened. This is expected for an off-canvas menu but should be covered by the interaction flow/accessibility behavior.

action_items: Ensure regression test fixtures select unused slots or clean prior TEST appointments before asserting successful booking.
critical_code_review_comments: The booking UI intentionally renders only available slots, so unavailable slots are not present as disabled controls; verify this meets the desired accessibility/product contract if disabled visibility is required.

success_rate.backend: 33% (1/3 existing focus tests; failures were occupied-slot conflicts)
success_rate.frontend: 100% core booking flow after opening mobile navigation

seed_data_creation: No seed data created; the browser flow created one appointment using the seeded patient account, which may affect fixed-slot regression tests.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Use patient@careflow.demo credentials from test_credentials.md. Public health and doctors endpoints passed. Mobile menu must be opened before clicking directory navigation. Avoid fixed slots already booked by prior runs.
rca of the issue: The two pytest failures were caused by persistent appointment state: both tests use predetermined doctor/date/time combinations, while prior runs and this run leave appointments in MongoDB. The API correctly returns 409 for occupied slots; tests need isolated or dynamically selected availability and cleanup.
